items.fact: The campaign has five chapters, and PC Gamer counts 91 story missions in total.
Push Square and Insider Gaming count 93 story missions across the five chapters, which is higher than PC Gamer's figure of 91. The totals differ because outlets treat optional missions differently.
Chapter 1 is based around the Leonida Keys and has 22 missions. Chapter 2 is set in Port Gellhorn, Chapters 3 and 4 in Vice City, and the short Chapter 5 covers Vice City and wider Leonida.
The story follows the duo Jason and Lucia through Leonida. Chapter 3 is where you can first switch between the two characters.
Chapter 2 ends with the mission Checking Out, once you reach the Move to Vice City point. Before then you should pay off the motel manager Linda, because your checkout fee grows the longer you wait.
Leonida is split into 5 counties. Locations named in guides include Key Lento in Mariana County, Vice City in Vice-Dale County, and North Leonard County.
There are 18 collectible card sets, and each set runs from common to rare cards. Cards sell at pawn shops, and rare ones fetch high prices.
The hidden magazines, books and comics collectible type has 27 pieces across the world, and four of them are inside Jason's starting house.
The Progress menu lists more than 250 animals to find and record. These include Rare, Discoverable and Legendary categories.
There are 60 birds to spot with the binoculars across Leonida. The game has 12 pieces of equipment in total, and they unlock gradually through the story.
The achievement list has 55 awards. They include meditating at all 18 spots, completing 3 card sets, and exploring all of Leonida.
Large bank vault robberies pay up to $200,000. They unlock near the end of Chapter 4 and need the side quest 'That's Where The Money Is...' plus two Payday Loan jobs.
From Chapter 3, Randy buys high-end stolen cars from a wish list of 18 sports cars, paying $30,000 or more each. Moses, from Chapter 2, pays far less and refuses cars with trackers.
There are 39 criminal hideouts across Leonida. Raiding these illegal operations is a strong early-game money source.
After the Island Dreams mission, Kenton in Key Lento unlocks underwater treasure dives that need a boat and scuba gear. Each haul sells for about $2,600.
Demolition derby races at Ambrosia Raceway pay over $3,000 on the oval track and about double on the figure-eight. You win by being the last car running, so you can rent a car and ram everyone.
Spend all the money in your stash before starting the Chapter 1 mission Tourist Trap, because you can never reach it again afterward.
Stealing cars is quiet only once you get the Slim Jim from the vehicle fence in Chapter 2's Moses mission. Before that you must smash windows, which draws attention.

Pre-order bonus vehicles unlock at set points. The Dinka Enduro bike and Crest Kayak are at Jason's house in Key Lento from Chapter 1, and the Shitzu Squalo boat is docked in Vice Beach from Chapter 4.
From Chapter 3 the Snap Gun opens locked doors without setting off alarms. Rob stores through the back door, then disable the alarm and destroy the security footage.

The first post-launch update, 01.002.002, came out on November 23, 2026. It fixed crashes, the weather not changing, broken autosaves, story phone calls that didn't trigger, wanted levels that wouldn't clear, the gym deadlift bar, and partners not handing over bags to sell to fences.
The update download is about 603.7 MB on PS5 and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X|S, and it rolled out in waves through the day.
The first patch's notes don't mention a glitch that forces first-person view or an Xbox glitch that unlocks 60fps, so both still work for now.
